distinguishing_features: Physically mitigates partial-discharge inception by inserting a low-permittivity porous pad that reduces the local electric field via permittivity grading, rather than monitoring or predicting degradation
Passive material-based field shaping at high-field barrier interfaces, with no sensing, dosing, or control loop
Targets fast-rising transient voltage spikes specifically (spike-aware void sizing) to keep E_local below inception threshold
Uses permittivity contrast/effective-medium void fraction to reduce E by ~40%, not an increase in dielectric thickness or strength
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to suppress partial-discharge inception at insulation defect sites during transient voltage spikes without increasing insulation thickness/thermal mass or reducing steady-state operating voltage margin.
parsed.viable_reason: The stated ~2x field reduction is derived from a capacitance-divider model that does not hold: inserting a low-permittivity layer beneath the high-field dielectric typically raises the field in the high-permittivity insulation, and a porous layer introduces gas voids whose own local fields promote, not suppress, partial discharge.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art performs passive permittivity-graded field shaping with engineered porosity to suppress PD at defects during voltage spikes, so the distinguishing mechanism is not a routine application of the closest art.
